title.title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
title.subtitle: Claim: every monotone solution of $\Delta u = u^3 - u$ on $\mathbb{R}^8$ is a flat $\tanh$ wall, with no extra assumption

plain: A smooth boundary between two phases, always rising in one direction: must it be a flat wall, up to 8D?

beats.text: The conjecture: a solution increasing in one direction is this one-dimensional wall
Without Savin's extra assumption, humans had reached dimension 4
The claim jumps to 8, where the conjecture ends

steps: Limits along the rising direction are stable, one dimension down
Every stable solution in seven dimensions is flat
A blow-down argument then flattens the original

achievement.label: De Giorgi's conjecture (1978), dimension 8
achievement.context: Key step: every stable solution in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is flat, with no energy-growth assumption
achievement.note: 97 pages, no Lean: the result our review trusts least

verify.detail: No Lean. Flatness of stable solutions in $\mathbb{R}^7$ rests on the paper alone
verify.ourCheck: We would not cite it as settled before an expert reads it

voice.text: A solution rising in one direction should be a flat wall. Humans reached dimension four.
Limits are stable one dimension down, where every stable solution is flat.
Claimed: dimension eight, the last case.

sources.ref: article, De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
sources.quote: De Giorgi conjectured in 1978 that a solution of the Allen–Cahn equation $\Delta u = u^3 - u$ that is monotone in one direction must be one-dimensional

sources.ref: article, De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
sources.quote: Ghoussoub and Gui proved dimension 2 (1998), Ambrosio and Cabré dimension 3 (2000), and Savin dimensions up to 8 (Annals 2009), but only under an extra assumption that $u \to \pm 1$ as the monotone coordinate goes to $\pm\infty$. Del Pino, Kowalczyk and Wei showed it fails from dimension 9 on (Annals 2011).
